---
title: "Sources, methods & corrections"
---

## Evidence before status

The original voter guide establishes what the author wrote. It does not establish passage, effective dates, enacted requirements, or implementation progress.

For results, use the [Maryland State Board of Elections](https://elections.maryland.gov/elections/2026/General_results/index.html) and identify whether a count is unofficial or certified. For governing provisions, start with [official ballot language and authorizing documents](https://elections.maryland.gov/elections/2026/ballot_questions.html). A ballot description is a starting point; detailed requirements need the enacted text.

For follow-up reporting, prioritize adopted budgets, ordinances, regulations, procurement and spending records, agency reports, meeting records, and court filings. News coverage provides leads and context; link the underlying records when available.

## Status definitions

| Field | Label | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Result | Awaiting certified results | No certified result has been entered for this publication. |
| Result | Passed — certified / Failed — certified | The cited official record establishes the certified outcome. |
| Result | Pending determination — certified | Certified counts have been entered, but the source does not establish a final disposition. |
| Implementation | Not assessed | Research is not yet sufficient to classify progress. |
| Implementation | Awaiting effective date | The sourced governing text establishes a future start date. |
| Implementation | In progress | Records document implementation steps underway. |
| Implementation | Implemented | Records establish the specified implementation milestone has been met; this is not a claim of policy success. |
| Implementation | Delayed / Challenged | Records document a missed applicable deadline or a formal challenge. |
| Implementation | Not applicable | The measure failed, or a documented reason makes implementation inapplicable. |

## Financial distinctions

**Authorization, issuance, appropriation, award, expenditure, and completion are different events.** Approval to borrow money does not show that it has been borrowed, spent, or delivered as a finished project. Amounts transcribed from the original guide must be checked before being used as verified financial findings.

## Analytical limits

Separate predictions, observations, and causal conclusions. A change after an election does not by itself show that a measure caused it. Report denominators, date ranges, missing records, and limitations alongside charts and calculations.

## Corrections

Keep the original publication date. Add a modification date and a dated correction explaining what changed when a factual claim changes. Update the source record and timeline. Until a public contact channel is added, use repository issues once this project has a GitHub home.

## Vote shares and margins

Vote shares are calculated from certified counts: **For ÷ (For + Against) × 100** and **Against ÷ (For + Against) × 100**. These exclude undervotes, invalid responses, and ballots with no vote recorded on the question. They are not turnout rates or shares of residents. Counts remain visible alongside percentages; shares are displayed to one decimal place, and a margin is a difference in percentage points.

Each measure has its own denominator. Maryland measures use statewide totals; Baltimore City measures use citywide totals. Do not compare raw counts across those electorates as if they covered the same population. The certified outcome is entered from the official record rather than inferred solely from a rounded percentage. Partial returns, voting-method subtotals, and precinct rows must not be entered as jurisdiction-wide totals.

The first results release will use jurisdiction-wide counts. A later precinct or ward analysis needs geographic identifiers, complete reporting coverage, and an explicit reconciliation to these totals. Never average precinct percentages to calculate the citywide percentage; sum the option counts first.
